config.description: M2 window 2026-11-19T01:29:31..01:36:28 (4 boots: P1 verbatim + --slot-save-path; +--cache-ram 16384 SKIPPED by the 24GiB RAM gate with the 5-guest set; --spec-type none; the d92ea9bb1 build) and the M2-FIX window 02:03:36..02:05:58 (2 boots of the P1+slot-save-path shape: an action-contract probe, then the save/park/restore live path and the fresh-process restore path), 40K-token reproducer fixture (36,979 tok, planted code), scratch port 8128, scope-isolated, watchdogs armed/disarmed, production stopped and live-verified around each window (both rc=0).

workload.fixture: seeded pseudo-text 40K (36,979 tok, planted code KGYVU); cold prefill; warm/identical followups; 120 s idle then followup; save (1.15 GB snapshot, target + MTP draft checkpoints) -> 40 s idle park -> explicit restore -> followup; fresh-process restore of the same file -> followup; n=1 per cell per boot

notes: Three findings. (1) Condition difference: at the measured Gen3 condition, 40K cold prefill is 581-583 tok/s (three engines, <0.4% spread) vs the 2026-11-18 M3 window's 414-416 tok/s for a 47K fixture at Gen3 x1 on the same engine class — the two conditions differ in BOTH negotiated width and prompt length, so this is reported as an observed condition difference, NOT an isolated width penalty (the earlier 'about 40% width tax' reading is retracted per the 2026-11-19 evening review; the isolated cell — the same 47K M3 fixture at the x4 condition — is planned next). Engine delta b12383 vs d92ea9bb1 ~0.3% (d92 stays a comparison build); MTP-off has no prefill effect. (2) The 40K-class disk tier is fast and correct end to end: a 1.15 GB / 37,001-token snapshot (target + MTP draft checkpoints) saves in 0.48 s, restores in 0.49-0.50 s both after a 40 s idle park in the same process and into a virgin process, and the followup reuses the restored state fully (36,990/4 tokens) with correct planted-code recall in <0.8 s total. The fast-persistence size boundary sits between 1.15 GB (works) and 4.19 GB (128K: silent full re-prefill, 531 s; the 1.8-3.3 GB RAM-tier loads fail outright) — the threshold is unmapped. (3) PCIe state-transition fingerprint (both windows, per-cell sampling, full coverage): on this stack (nvidia 595.71.05 on a Proxmox VE 9.2 / kernel 7.0.14 host) every power-on negotiates Gen3 x16/x4, every model load lands both links at Gen1 (width preserved), every unload/stop re-trains to Gen3 — reproducibly, with no kernel PCIe events in any direction. This is a reliable observed fingerprint, NOT an established driver defect: all observations were quiescent, and NVIDIA link management reduces generation while idle, so the post-load state is consistent with idle power management; whether it persists under sustained traffic is unmeasured (the active-traffic sampling test — no reboot, no kernel parameters — is the planned discriminator; the pcie_aspm=off proposal is withdrawn per review). The 01:29 window's save-erase-restore cells were voided by a harness bug (the b12383 save action requires a JSON {filename} body; empty body = 400; erase clears registered cache entries, not the slot's live KV) and were re-run correctly in M2-FIX. A harness-state failure (stale armed-watchdog marker after a killed window) left production down ~10 min (01:56-02:06) before manual restore; no data loss; the fix (pre-stop preflight, transactional stop-and-arm, supervisor early recovery) is being implemented before the next window.
